evidence.title: 부대관리훈령 별표 31 체력검정 기준 (남군)
evidence.supports: Test items (2-min push-ups, 2-min sit-ups, 3km run) and age-based grade-1 thresholds.

evidence.title: FM 7-22 Holistic Health and Fitness
evidence.supports: Military physical training structure: aerobic, muscular strength/endurance, core, mobility and recovery components; foot marching as a trained task.

evidence.title: Soldier load carriage: historical, physiological, biomechanical, and medical aspects
evidence.source: Knapik JJ, Reynolds KL, Harman E. Military Medicine. 2004;169(1):45-56
evidence.supports: Load carriage performance relates to aerobic fitness and lower-body/trunk strength; progressive loaded marching as part of training.

evidence.title: A systematic review of the effects of physical training on load carriage performance
evidence.source: Knapik JJ, Harman EA, Steelman RA, Graham BS. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research. 2012;26(2):585-597
evidence.supports: Combined resistance and aerobic training, with or without loaded marching, improves load carriage performance.

evidence.title: Quantity and quality of exercise for developing and maintaining cardiorespiratory, musculoskeletal, and neuromotor fitness in apparently healthy adults (ACSM Position Stand)
evidence.source: Garber CE, et al. Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise. 2011;43(7):1334-1359
evidence.supports: Frequency/volume ranges for aerobic and resistance exercise; gradual progression of exercise volume.

evidence.title: NSCA's Essentials of Tactical Strength and Conditioning
evidence.source: Alvar BA, Sell K, Deuster PA (eds). Human Kinetics, 2017
evidence.supports: Exercise selection for tactical populations: lower-body strength, trunk stability, loaded carries, interval and continuous running, recovery practices.
